groups.note: Arnold omits the repeated statement about the destruction of family and caste rites; note 1 explicitly records omitted repetitionary lines.
Arnold interweaves the difficulty of renunciation and attaining Brahman (5.6) with the pure-hearted yogin's description (5.7).

Arnold omits the five verses about departure paths and times. The source marks the gap with an ellipsis and an incorrectly repeated [FN#14]; translator note 15 explains the omitted ten Sanskrit lines.
Arnold combines and reorders the two verses' lists of qualities; retain their common source span.
Arnold interweaves the named warriors (11.26) with their entry into the jaws (11.27).

Arnold omits the verse about sages, hymns, and Brahma-sutra reasoning. The source ellipsis and note 28 explicitly mark the omitted two Sanskrit lines. Canonical numbering excludes Arjuna's alternate opening question.
Arnold omits the verse about memory, knowledge, and the Vedas; translator note 31 explicitly says he omits a verse at this point.

The source ends its rendering after the three gates and liberation from them. Note 33 says 'ten concluding shlokas'; the actual gap in the project's standard 24-verse chapter is 16.23–16.24. Preserve this discrepancy without adding text.
Arnold ends the chapter after the three kinds of gifts. Note 37 explicitly omits the concluding shlokas, corresponding to canonical 17.23–17.28.
